page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range, with read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 553.05 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 62.15 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform steadily, as evidenced by average scores in Passmark encryption and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, the instance exhibits limitations in complex AI workloads, showing weak performance in prompt processing for medium-sized 7B LLM models.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density, the c2d-highmem-8 offers a balanced qualitative cost-efficiency profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The absence of a GPU and local SSDs makes it less suitable for heavy machine learning training or high-IOPS database storage. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, enterprise web serving, and moderate data processing pipelines.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, making it a dedicated resource for memory-intensive workloads rather than storage-heavy or graphics-accelerated tasks. It is highly suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and general-purpose memory-bound enterprise applications.
